Attempt 1 (review failed):
Critical issues:
[Claude] CRITICAL: Code uses non-null assertions (`!`) on optional methods of dynamically imported module without validation. If `./math.js` doesn't export all required methods (add, sub, mul, div), calling them will crash with "Cannot read property of undefined" at runtime.
[Copilot] CRITICAL: `compute()` has no `default` case in the switch — an invalid `op` silently returns `undefined` despite the `Promise<number>` return type. Any caller relying on the numeric result will get `undefined` with no error thrown.
[Copilot] CRITICAL: Division by zero is silently swallowed — `div: (x,y) => x / y` returns `Infinity` (or `NaN` for `0/0`) without any error. Callers receive a non-finite number with no indication of failure, risking silent data corruption downstream.
[Copilot] CRITICAL: `await import("./math.js")` loads and executes an arbitrary file from the working directory. If an attacker can place a malicious `math.js` alongside the binary (e.g., in a writable deploy dir), this is remote code execution. The project rules also explicitly prohibit inline dynamic imports.
[Codex] CRITICAL: `packages/orchestrator/src/math-cli.ts:31` contains a raw newline inside a double-quoted string literal (`console.error("Usage: ... <b>` on one line, `ops: ...")` on the next), which is a syntax error in TS/JS and prevents the file from compiling or running at all.

Attempt 1 (review failed):
Critical issues:
[Gemini] CRITICAL: The `wordFreq` function uses a plain object (`{}`) as a map for word counts. If the input text contains words that match `Object.prototype` properties (e.g., "constructor", "toString", "hasOwnProperty"), the function will return incorrect values (strings instead of numbers) because `counts[t]` will initially retrieve the prototype's function instead of `undefined`. This should be fixed by using `Object.create(null)` or a `Map`.
